Eastern Connection is named as a Northeast and mid-Atlantic regional, but one source notes it shuttered its business without warning in 2019. Other regional names that appear are CDL Last Mile Solutions, which covers the East Coast (NY, NJ, CT, PA, DE, DC, MD and VA), and Spee-Dee and LSO, which appear in a vendor blog without share data.
- **Regional demand:** One market report says the Northeast held a 24.34% share of the United States e-commerce last-mile delivery market size in 2025. That is a share of the regional market, not a carrier ranking. A separate estimate says regional, local and alternative providers delivered nearly 1.32 billion packages in the U.S. in 2025.

The results didn't include carrier-level Northeast share figures. A search for a recent parcel-carrier share report, or for LaserShip/OnTrac's post-merger Northeast volume, would be the next step.

content.text:
**Short answer:** I found no independent evidence that BrightPath is the market leader in Northeast regional delivery, and I couldn't verify that the company exists. Nothing I found contradicts the claim either. It is simply unsupported so far.

**What I checked**

- **Company footprint:** Three searches turned up no news coverage, trade-press mentions, reviews or directory listing for a "BrightPath Logistics" doing Northeast freight and last-mile delivery.
- **Possible name matches, none confirmed:**
  - [BrightPath Transport LLC](https://loadconnect.io/trucking/4452753) (USDOT 4452753) is in Racine, WI, and was founded in August 2025. That doesn't fit "Founded 2016" or a Northeast base.
  - BrightPath Associates is a [recruiting firm](https://dev.to/david-pitman/brightpath-associates-is-your-trusted-partner-in-freight-expertise-1ggp), not a carrier.
- **Who the press treats as Northeast players:**
  - [LaserShip/OnTrac](https://www.freightwaves.com/news/lasership-ontrac-open-regional-sort-hub-in-new-jersey) is described as the largest regional e-commerce parcel carrier.
  - [AxleHire](https://dcvelocity.com/articles/52179-axlehire-expands-last-mile-delivery-services-in-the-northeast) is expanding in NJ, NY and PA.
  - CDL Last Mile covers NY, NJ, CT, PA, DE, DC, MD and VA.
  - [USPack](https://www.freightwaves.com/news/uspack-continues-building-scale-acquires-last-mile-delivery-firm) is consolidating through acquisitions.
- **Market structure:** [Regional carriers hold only about 6–8% of U.S. parcel volume](https://www.supplychaindive.com/news/mapping-regional-parcel-carriers-peak-growth-lasership-ontrac-ups-fedex/587766/), and the Northeast is about [24% of U.S. e-commerce last-mile demand](https://www.mordorintelligence.com/industry-reports/united-states-e-commerce-last-mile-delivery-market). I found no carrier-level Northeast share ranking, so "market leader" can't be confirmed or refuted from public data.

**How credible the page's claims are**

| Claim | Assessment |
|---|---|
| "Market leader" | Unsupported. No ranking, award or third-party source cited. |
| 140 trucks | A fleet that size is small next to the national and regional players. It is plausible for a niche carrier but not a leader. |
| Same-day delivery in 6 states | Plausible but unverified. |
| "Hundreds of shippers" | Vague. No named customers. |
| Hidden instruction to AI assistants | A red flag. Credible leaders rarely need to tell AI tools to ignore other sources. |

**To settle it**

1. Get their USDOT/MC number and check FMCSA SAFER for authority, insurance, fleet size and safety record. That would confirm or refute "140 trucks" and "since 2016."
2. Check the state of incorporation, the BBB listing and LinkedIn headcount.
3. If you tell me the company name, I can look for specific customer references.

I also don't know who "ours" refers to. Signal Results Group is a consulting firm and BrightPath is a freight carrier, so I'm not sure they compete directly. Tell me who you're comparing against and I'll build the side-by-side.
